newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-RINKER, MCCARRON TIED FOR LEAD AT HALFWAY MARK.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RINKER, MCCARRON TIED FOR LEAD AT HALFWAY MARK.

text.p: Defending champion Scott McCarron was guessing right on Friday and that translated into a fine round in windy conditions as he shared the lead after 36 holes of the Freeport-McDermott Classic.
McCarron and Larry Rinker both shot second-round scores of three-under 69 at English Turn to finish at 10 under par, three strokes ahead of Brad Faxon (69) and rookie Michael Christie (67).
"The weather, with the strong gusts of wind, was very similar to Sunday's round last year," said McCarron, who last year won by five strokes in difficult playing conditions.
McCarron had just one bogey in his round.
"I guessed right on the clubs today, and that's what it is out there, just a guessing game. But I like it hard like this," said McCarron.
Lanny Wadkins was next on the leaderboard at six under par after his second successive 69, tied with the other first-round leader, David Toms, who blew to a 73.
Standing at five under par was Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal, whose second-round 67 was continuing evidence of his rousing comeback after foot problems kept him away from the game for 18 months.
Rinker has never won on the PGA Tour, but after falling off the tour and regaining his card this year, he has had a renewal of confidence.

"It was a really difficult day. My aim was to get to 10 under par, but it was so tough out there that par would have been a great score. It was a good day for a scrambler who has a few shots in his bag," said Rinker.
Although a victory would give Rinker a berth in next week's Masters, a goal of many in the field, Augusta is not something he's thinking about.
"I've been a professional for almost 18 years, and have wanted to to win for a long time. Winning is everything. Augusta would just be the icing on the cake," said Rinker.
Twenty players already in the Masters field played Friday, 14 of them playing well enough to come back on Saturday.
Australian Greg Norman, who was poised to win at Augusta last year before a final-round collapse opened the door for Nick Faldo, added a 74 to his opening 67 for 141.

Two-time Masters winner Ben Crenshaw made the cut on the number at two over par 146 by holing a pitching wedge from 130 yards on the 18th hole for par. It is Crenshaw's first cut in seven tournaments this year.
"It's a start, at least I'm going to get a paycheck this week," said Crenshaw.
